syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the structure of a typical anther and the wall layers of a microsporangium with their functions.
Explain how pollen mother cells form microspore tetrads by meiosis and work out the ploidy of the products.
Describe the two-layered wall and the two- or three-celled contents of a mature pollen grain.

topics.title: The pistil, ovule and embryo sac

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the parts of a typical angiosperm ovule such as funicle, hilum, integuments, micropyle, chalaza and nucellus.
Explain megasporogenesis and monosporic development of the embryo sac, including the ploidy of the cells involved.
Describe the 7-celled, 8-nucleate organisation of the mature embryo sac formed by free-nuclear mitosis.
Distinguish autogamy, geitonogamy and xenogamy, and chasmogamous from cleistogamous flowers.
Relate the features of wind- and water-pollinated flowers to the way their pollen is carried.
Explain how animal-pollinated flowers attract and reward pollinators, including plant-pollinator mutualism.

topics.title: Outbreeding devices, pollen-pistil interaction and artificial hybridisation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the devices that discourage self-pollination, including self-incompatibility, monoecy and dioecy.
Describe pollen recognition by the pistil and the path of the pollen tube to the synergid.
Explain emasculation and bagging and their order in a crop-improvement cross.
Identify the nuclei that take part in syngamy and in triple fusion inside the embryo sac.
Explain why fertilisation in angiosperms is called double fertilisation and work out the ploidy of its products.
Explain free-nuclear and cellular endosperm development and why endosperm forms before the embryo.
Compare the parts of dicotyledonous and monocotyledonous (grass) embryos.
Distinguish albuminous from non-albuminous seeds and identify perisperm and seed coats.
Explain the development of true, false and parthenocarpic fruits from floral parts.
Evaluate the role of dehydration, dormancy and viability of seeds in survival and agriculture.
Explain apomixis as asexual seed formation and its importance for hybrid seed production.
Explain how nucellar cells give rise to multiple embryos in a seed and the genetic nature of such embryos.
Describe the location and internal organisation of the testis, including seminiferous tubules, Sertoli cells and Leydig cells.
Trace the path of sperms through the male accessory ducts and state the role of the accessory glands and seminal plasma.
Describe the structure and functions of the ovaries, oviducts, uterus and external genitalia.
Describe the structure of the mammary gland and the path of milk from the alveoli to the nipple.
Explain the stages of spermatogenesis, the chromosome number at each stage and its hormonal control.
Relate the parts of a human sperm to their functions and state the criteria for normal fertility.
Explain the stages of oogenesis and compare it with spermatogenesis.
Describe the menstrual, follicular, ovulatory and luteal phases and the changes in the ovary and uterus.
Explain how pituitary and ovarian hormones regulate ovulation and the maintenance of the endometrium.
Explain where and how fertilisation occurs and how entry of additional sperms is blocked.
Explain why the sex of a baby is determined by the sperm that fertilises the ovum.
Describe cleavage, the formation of the morula and blastocyst, and implantation.
Describe the formation and functions of the placenta and the hormones of pregnancy.
Describe germ layer formation and the major features of foetal development during pregnancy.
Explain the neuroendocrine mechanism of parturition, including the role of oxytocin.
Explain lactation and the importance of colostrum for the new-born.
Define reproductive health as total well-being in all aspects of reproduction and identify indicators of its improvement.
Describe India's family planning and RCH programmes and the role of awareness and sex education.
Explain what amniocentesis is, its legitimate use and why its use for sex determination is banned.

topics.title: Population stabilisation and the ideal contraceptive

concepts.learning_objective: State the reasons for rapid population growth and interpret population growth rates.
Identify the measures taken in India to check population growth.
List the features of an ideal contraceptive and evaluate methods against them.

topics.title: Natural and barrier methods of contraception

concepts.learning_objective: Explain periodic abstinence, withdrawal and lactational amenorrhoea and their limitations.
Describe condoms, diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults and how they prevent conception.

topics.title: IUDs, hormonal and surgical methods of contraception

concepts.learning_objective: Classify IUDs and explain how they prevent conception.
Explain the use and action of oral pills, injectables, implants and emergency contraceptives.
Distinguish vasectomy and tubectomy and explain how sterilisation prevents conception.
Define MTP and state the reasons for which it is performed.
Apply the conditions of the MTP (Amendment) Act, 2017 to given situations.
Explain when MTP is relatively safe and identify its dangerous misuses.
Name common STIs, their modes of transmission and which of them are not completely curable.
Explain why STIs often go untreated and the complications that may follow.
State the simple principles that help prevent STIs.
Define infertility and state its possible causes in either partner.
Explain IVF followed by embryo transfer through ZIFT and IUT.
Distinguish GIFT, ICSI and artificial insemination and choose the suitable one for a case.

topics.title: Mendel's experiments and inheritance of one gene

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how Mendel used true-breeding pea lines with seven pairs of contrasting traits to study inheritance.
Work out the phenotypic and genotypic ratios of a monohybrid cross using the laws of dominance and segregation.
Use a test cross with the recessive parent to find the genotype of a plant showing the dominant phenotype.

topics.title: Incomplete dominance, co-dominance and multiple alleles

concepts.learning_objective: Explain incomplete dominance with the snapdragon flower colour example and its 1:2:1 F2 ratio.
Explain co-dominance using the ABO blood group alleles and work out possible blood groups of offspring.
Explain why multiple alleles of a gene can be recognised only through population studies.

topics.title: Inheritance of two genes and the chromosomal theory

concepts.learning_objective: Derive the 9:3:3:1 dihybrid ratio and apply the law of independent assortment to gamete and offspring calculations.
Relate the behaviour of chromosomes in meiosis to Mendel's laws as proposed by Sutton and Boveri.
Explain how linkage of genes on the same chromosome changes dihybrid ratios and how recombination arises.
Use recombination frequency as a measure of the distance between genes on a chromosome.
Explain the additive effect of alleles in polygenic traits such as human skin colour.
Explain how a single gene such as the one mutated in phenylketonuria can show multiple phenotypic effects.
Compare XO, XY and ZW mechanisms of sex determination and the ideas of male and female heterogamety.
Explain why the sperm decides the sex of a human child and why each birth has a 50 per cent chance of either sex.
Describe the haplodiploid sex-determination system of the honey bee and its consequences.
Distinguish point mutations, frame-shift mutations and chromosomal aberrations and identify mutagens.
Use pedigree analysis to infer whether a human trait is dominant or recessive, autosomal or sex-linked.
Predict the inheritance of X-linked recessive disorders such as colour blindness and haemophilia.
Explain the genetic basis of sickle-cell anaemia, phenylketonuria and thalassemia.
Relate Down's, Klinefelter's and Turner's syndromes to aneuploidy and their karyotypes.

topics.title: The DNA: Structure of the Polynucleotide Chain and Double Helix

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the components of a nucleotide and the linkages that form a nucleoside, nucleotide and polynucleotide chain.
Explain the salient features of the Watson-Crick double helix, including base pairing, Chargaff's rule and helix dimensions.
Explain how negatively charged DNA is packaged with positively charged histones into nucleosomes and chromatin.
Distinguish euchromatin from heterochromatin and relate packaging to transcriptional activity.

topics.title: The Search for Genetic Material and the RNA World

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the experiments of Griffith and of Avery, MacLeod and McCarty on the transforming principle.
Explain how Hershey and Chase used radioactive phosphorus and sulfur to prove that DNA is the genetic material.
Evaluate DNA and RNA against the criteria for a genetic material and explain why RNA is regarded as the first genetic material.
Interpret the Meselson and Stahl experiment as proof of semiconservative DNA replication.
Describe the roles of DNA polymerase, DNA ligase, the replication fork and the origin of replication.
Identify the promoter, structural gene, terminator, template strand and coding strand of a transcription unit.
Compare transcription in bacteria and eukaryotes, including the RNA polymerases and the sigma and rho factors.
Explain split genes and the splicing, capping and tailing of hnRNA.
State and apply the salient features of the genetic code.
Distinguish point mutations from frameshift insertion and deletion mutations and predict their effect.
Describe the structure and adapter role of tRNA.

topics.title: Translation and Regulation of Gene Expression

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the charging of tRNA and the initiation, elongation and termination of translation on the ribosome.
Explain the negative regulation of the lac operon by its repressor and inducer.

topics.title: Human Genome Project and DNA Fingerprinting

concepts.learning_objective: State the goals, methods and salient findings of the Human Genome Project.
Explain the steps and the polymorphism basis of DNA fingerprinting using VNTR probes.
Describe the formation of the universe and the conditions on early earth before life appeared.
Explain how Pasteur's experiments rejected spontaneous generation and established that life comes from pre-existing life.
Explain the Oparin-Haldane hypothesis of chemical evolution and the significance of Miller's experiment.

topics.title: Evolution of Life Forms - A Theory

concepts.learning_objective: State the three connotations of the theory of special creation and why they were challenged.
Explain Darwin's idea of natural selection and fitness as reproductive fitness.
Explain paleontological evidence and the embryological argument for evolution and its rejection.
Distinguish homologous and analogous structures as results of divergent and convergent evolution.
Interpret industrial melanism and resistance to pesticides and antibiotics as evidence of natural selection.
Define adaptive radiation using Darwin's finches and Australian marsupials as examples.
Explain how parallel radiations of Australian marsupials and placental mammals illustrate convergent evolution.

topics.title: Biological Evolution and Mechanism of Evolution

concepts.learning_objective: Explain branching descent and natural selection, and the observations on which Darwin based them.
Describe Lamarck's theory of use and disuse of organs and inheritance of acquired characters.
Contrast de Vries' mutation theory (saltation) with Darwinian variation.
Apply the Hardy-Weinberg equation to calculate allele and genotype frequencies.
Identify the factors that disturb Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, including gene flow, genetic drift and founder effect.
Distinguish stabilising, directional and disruptive selection.
Trace the sequence from invertebrates and lobefins to amphibians, reptiles and mammals.
Explain the rise of mammals and the effect of continental drift on their distribution.
Describe Dryopithecus, Ramapithecus, Australopithecines and Homo habilis.
Compare the brain capacities and habits of Homo habilis, Homo erectus and Neanderthal man.
Outline the rise of modern Homo sapiens, cave art and agriculture.

topics.title: Common diseases in humans and their prevention

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the pathogens, symptoms, transmission and diagnosis of typhoid, pneumonia and the common cold.
Describe the life cycle of Plasmodium in its two hosts and explain the cause of malarial fever.
Relate amoebiasis, ascariasis, filariasis and ringworm to their pathogens and to measures of hygiene and vector control.
Classify the physical, physiological, cellular and cytokine barriers of innate immunity.
Distinguish the primary and secondary immune responses on the basis of immunological memory.
Describe the H2L2 structure of antibodies and distinguish humoral from cell-mediated immunity.
Distinguish active from passive immunity with natural and artificial examples.
Explain how vaccines and antitoxins protect the body, using the memory of the immune system.
State how recombinant DNA technology is used to produce vaccines such as the hepatitis B vaccine.

topics.title: Allergies, auto-immunity and the lymphoid organs

concepts.learning_objective: Explain allergy as an exaggerated IgE response with histamine release from mast cells.
Explain auto-immune disease as an immune attack on self-cells, with an example.
Distinguish primary from secondary lymphoid organs and state their roles.
Identify the routes by which HIV is transmitted and the ways by which it is not.
Explain how HIV replicates in macrophages and helper T-lymphocytes and causes immunodeficiency.
State the diagnosis, treatment limits and preventive measures for AIDS.
Distinguish cancer cells from normal cells and benign from malignant tumors, and explain metastasis.
Classify physical, chemical and biological carcinogens and explain the role of oncogenes.
Describe methods of detecting and treating cancer, including biological response modifiers.
Relate opioids, cannabinoids and coca alkaloids to their sources, receptors and effects.
Explain the physiological effects and health risks of nicotine and tobacco smoke.

topics.title: Adolescence, addiction and prevention of drug abuse

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish addiction from dependence and explain the role of tolerance.
Describe the short-term and long-term effects of drug, alcohol and steroid abuse.
Suggest measures for preventing and controlling drug and alcohol abuse among adolescents.
Explain how lactic acid bacteria convert milk into curd and improve its nutritional value.
Describe the role of microbes in fermenting dough and traditional foods and drinks.
Relate the texture and flavour of different cheeses to the specific microbes used.
Describe the use of brewer's yeast in producing distilled and undistilled alcoholic beverages.
Explain what antibiotics are and outline the discovery and development of penicillin.

topics.title: Chemicals, enzymes and other bioactive molecules

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the microbes used for commercial production of organic acids and ethanol.
State the uses of microbial enzymes such as lipases, pectinases, proteases and streptokinase.
Describe the sources and uses of cyclosporin A and statins.
Describe the physical steps of primary sewage treatment.
Explain biological secondary treatment and interpret BOD as a measure of organic pollution.
Explain the fate of activated sludge and the role of anaerobic sludge digesters.
Explain the role of methanogens in producing methane from cellulosic material.
Describe the structure and working of a gobar gas plant.
Explain the principle of biological pest control in organic farming.
Explain how Bacillus thuringiensis is used to control caterpillars.
Describe Trichoderma and baculoviruses as specific biocontrol agents.
Distinguish between symbiotic and free-living nitrogen-fixing bacteria used as biofertilisers.
Explain the benefits of mycorrhizal associations to plants.
Describe the role of cyanobacteria as biofertilisers in paddy fields.

topics.title: Principles of biotechnology and the first recombinant DNA

concepts.learning_objective: Describe genetic engineering and bioprocess engineering as the two core techniques of modern biotechnology.
Explain why an alien piece of DNA must be linked to an origin of replication to multiply in a host.
Describe how Cohen and Boyer constructed and cloned the first recombinant DNA.
Explain the naming convention of restriction enzymes and distinguish endonucleases from exonucleases.
Explain how restriction enzymes recognise palindromic sequences and produce sticky ends.

topics.title: Separation and isolation of DNA fragments by gel electrophoresis

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how agarose gel electrophoresis separates DNA fragments according to size.
Describe how separated DNA bands are visualised and recovered from the gel.
Describe the role of the origin of replication, selectable marker and cloning sites in a vector.
Explain how insertional inactivation is used to select recombinants from non-recombinants.
Explain how disarmed Ti plasmids and retroviruses are used as vectors in plants and animals.

topics.title: Competent host and introducing recombinant DNA into host cells

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how bacterial cells are made competent to take up recombinant DNA.
Distinguish micro-injection, biolistics and disarmed pathogen vectors as methods of gene transfer.
Explain how a selectable marker allows only transformed cells to grow.

topics.title: Isolating and cutting DNA, and amplification by PCR

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the steps used to isolate pure DNA from cells.
Explain the steps of PCR and the role of primers and thermostable DNA polymerase.

topics.title: Obtaining the foreign gene product and downstream processing

concepts.learning_objective: Define a recombinant protein and explain why continuous culture improves yield.
Describe the features and advantages of stirred-tank bioreactors for large-scale production.
Describe the steps of downstream processing before a product is marketed.

topics.title: Tissue culture, micropropagation and somatic hybridisation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain totipotency and state the components of a plant tissue culture medium.
Describe micropropagation, somaclones and the raising of virus-free plants from meristems.
Outline how protoplast fusion produces somatic hybrids such as the pomato.

topics.title: Genetically modified crops and Bt cotton

concepts.learning_objective: List the ways in which genetic modification has improved crop plants.
Explain how the Bt protoxin is activated in the insect gut and kills the insect.
Relate specific cry genes to the insect pests they control.

topics.title: Pest resistant plants through RNA interference

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how a complementary dsRNA silences a specific mRNA in RNA interference.
Describe how RNAi was used to protect tobacco roots from Meloidogyne incognita.
State the advantages of recombinant therapeutics over products from non-human sources.
Describe the two-chain structure of insulin and the removal of the C peptide from pro-insulin.
Explain how Eli Lilly produced human insulin in E. coli.
Define gene therapy and state how it corrects a genetic defect.
Describe the treatment options for adenosine deaminase deficiency, including gene therapy.
Explain how PCR allows detection of a pathogen at very low concentration.
Interpret the use of a radioactive probe and autoradiography to detect a mutated gene.
State the antigen-antibody principle of ELISA and what it detects.
Define transgenic animals and give examples of them.
Match the uses of transgenic animals with suitable examples.
State the need for regulating GM research and the role of GEAC.
Evaluate patent disputes such as Basmati and explain biopiracy.
Define a population and identify the attributes a population has but an individual does not.
Calculate per capita birth and death rates of a population.
Interpret the shape of an age pyramid as growing, stable or declining population.
Choose numbers, per cent cover or biomass as the meaningful measure of population density.
Explain how relative densities and indirect evidence are used to estimate population size.
Apply Nt+1 = Nt + [(B + I) - (D + E)] to predict change in population density.
Describe exponential growth (dN/dt = rN) and its J-shaped curve and calculate r.
Explain logistic growth, its sigmoid curve and the role of carrying capacity K.
Compare breeding once versus many times and many small versus few large offspring.
State that populations evolve to maximise Darwinian fitness (high r) in their habitat.
Classify interspecific interactions using +, - and 0 signs for the two species.
Explain the roles of predators in energy transfer, prey control and species diversity.
Describe defences of prey animals and plants against predators and herbivores.
Explain competition, competitive release and Gause's Competitive Exclusion Principle.
Explain how resource partitioning allows competing species to co-exist.
Describe ectoparasites, endoparasites, brood parasitism and parasitic adaptations.
Identify commensal interactions such as orchid-mango and cattle egret-cattle.
Explain mutualism and co-evolution using lichens, mycorrhizae, fig-wasp and Ophrys.
Identify the abiotic, autotrophic, consumer and decomposer components of an ecosystem such as a pond.
Explain species composition and stratification as structural features of an ecosystem.
Describe how the components of an ecosystem function as a unit through energy flow and recycling of matter.
Define primary production, GPP and NPP and relate them using GPP - R = NPP.
Define secondary productivity as the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers.
Explain why primary productivity varies between ecosystems, including the low productivity of oceans.
Describe fragmentation, leaching and catabolism as steps in the decomposition of detritus.
Explain the formation and role of humus and the release of nutrients by mineralisation.
Analyse how the chemical nature of detritus and climatic factors control the rate of decomposition.
State the share of solar radiation that is PAR and the fraction of PAR captured by plants.
Distinguish the grazing food chain from the detritus food chain and explain how they form a food web.
Apply the 10 per cent law and the idea of standing crop to energy transfer between trophic levels.
Describe pyramids of number, biomass and energy and explain why the energy pyramid is always upright.
Explain the occurrence of inverted pyramids, such as the pyramid of biomass in the sea.
Evaluate the limitations of ecological pyramids, such as species occupying more than one trophic level.
Distinguish genetic, species and ecological diversity with examples from India.

topics.title: How many species are there on earth and in India

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how the global number of species is estimated and how recorded species are distributed among taxa.
Explain why India is a mega diversity country and estimate its undiscovered species.
Explain the latitudinal gradient in species diversity and the hypotheses for tropical richness.
Interpret the species-area relationship log S = log C + Z log A and the meaning of Z.

topics.title: Importance of species diversity to the ecosystem

concepts.learning_objective: Relate species richness to the stability and productivity of a community using Tilman's findings.
Use Paul Ehrlich's rivet popper analogy to explain the effect of species loss on ecosystems.
Compare present extinction rates with past mass extinctions and state their consequences.
Identify the four major causes of biodiversity loss and apply them to examples.
Distinguish narrowly and broadly utilitarian reasons for conserving biodiversity.
State the ethical argument for conserving every species.
Explain in situ conservation through protected areas and sacred groves.
Define biodiversity hotspots and identify those covering India.
Describe ex situ conservation methods and when they are needed.
